revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Treasure Map Mirror Twins
revealWordProblem.text: Captain Vega buries a chest at (-6, 4) on her treasure map. She wants to bury a decoy chest that is a mirror image of the real one, reflected across the y-axis, so raiders searching the wrong side will still find a clue. What are the coordinates of the decoy chest, and how far is it from the y-axis?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Reflecting across the y-axis flips the sign of the x-coordinate and keeps the y-coordinate the same, so (-6, 4) becomes (6, 4). The original chest is |-6| = 6 units from the y-axis, and the decoy is also 6 units from the y-axis, just on the opposite side. The decoy chest is at (6, 4), exactly 6 units from the y-axis.

vocabulary.definition: Use a number line to decide which integers are greater or less and place them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Usar una recta numérica para decidir cuáles enteros son mayores o menores y colocarlos en orden.
vocabulary.cloze: On a number line, the number farther to the ___ is always less.

examples.why: Position on the line decides the comparison.
For negatives, a bigger digit means a smaller value.

vocabulary.definition: A straight line where numbers are placed in order; numbers get smaller to the left and larger to the right.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una recta donde los números se colocan en orden; los números son menores a la izquierda y mayores a la derecha.
vocabulary.cloze: To plot integers in order, place them on a ___.

examples.text: A line with -3, 0 and 3 marked in order
examples.why: Values placed in order, left to right, around 0.

examples.text: Three numbers listed in a column
examples.why: A list has no positions, so it shows no order or distance.

vocabulary.definition: To see if a number is bigger, smaller, or equal to another.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Ver si un número es mayor, menor o igual que otro.
vocabulary.visual: -3 < 2 because -3 is farther left on the number line than 2
vocabulary.cloze: To decide which number is larger or smaller is to ___ them.

examples.why: It judges one value against another.
Writing both down decides nothing.

vocabulary.definition: To arrange numbers by size, from least to greatest or greatest to least.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Acomodar números por tamaño, de menor a mayor o de mayor a menor.
vocabulary.visual: Least to greatest: -5, -2, 0, 3, 7 (left to right on the number line)
vocabulary.cloze: To arrange numbers from least to greatest or greatest to least is to ___ them.

examples.why: The values are arranged by size.
No arrangement by size has happened.

vocabulary.definition: The > sign, showing one number is bigger.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El signo >, que muestra que un número es mayor.
vocabulary.visual: 4 > -1 because 4 is to the right of -1 on the number line
vocabulary.cloze: On a number line, a number farther to the right is ___ another number.

examples.why: -3 is farther right on the line, so it is greater.
-8 is farther left, which makes it the smaller value.

vocabulary.definition: The < sign, showing one number is smaller.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El signo <, que muestra que un número es menor.
vocabulary.visual: -6 < -2 because -6 is farther left — it is farther from zero
vocabulary.cloze: On a number line, a number farther to the left is ___ another number.

examples.why: -15 sits farther left, so it is the lesser value.
-20 is deeper still, so this reverses the order.

vocabulary.definition: A whole number smaller than zero, like -5.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número entero menor que cero, como -5.
vocabulary.visual: -4 is 4 units to the LEFT of zero on the number line
vocabulary.cloze: An integer less than zero, like −6, is a ___.

examples.why: It is an integer less than zero.
It is greater than zero, so it is positive.

vocabulary.definition: Whole numbers and their opposites, like -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números enteros y sus opuestos, como -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A whole number or its opposite is an ___.

examples.why: Whole numbers, their opposites, and zero.
A number between two whole numbers is not an integer.

vocabulary.termEs: Representar en el plano de coordenadas
vocabulary.definition: Plot a point by moving horizontally to its x-coordinate and vertically to its y-coordinate.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Ubicar un punto moviéndose horizontalmente hasta su coordenada x y verticalmente hasta su coordenada y.
vocabulary.visual: For (3, −2), move right 3 and down 2.
vocabulary.cloze: Plot a point by moving to its ___-coordinate first, then its ___-coordinate.

examples.why: The x move comes first, always.
That plots (2, 5), a different point.

vocabulary.termEs: Distancia en el plano de coordenadas
vocabulary.definition: The positive space between points, found from the absolute difference of coordinates on a horizontal or vertical line.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio positivo entre puntos, que se halla con la diferencia absoluta de las coordenadas en una línea horizontal o vertical.
vocabulary.cloze: When two points share a coordinate, the distance is the ___ ___ of the difference.

examples.why: Same y, so subtract the x-values and take the absolute value.
Dropping the negative sign loses the whole left-hand span.

vocabulary.definition: A corner point of a polygon, named by an ordered pair on the coordinate plane.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un punto de esquina de un polígono, nombrado por un par ordenado en el plano de coordenadas.
vocabulary.visual: The park's corner at (2, 4) — one corner, named by an ordered pair.
vocabulary.cloze: A corner point of a polygon, named by an ordered pair, is a ___.

examples.text: (5, 4), where two sides of the park meet
examples.why: It is a corner, and a coordinate pair names it.
That is a side; a vertex is the point where sides meet.

vocabulary.term: Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants
vocabulary.termEs: Pares ordenados en los cuatro cuadrantes
vocabulary.definition: Points written as (x, y) whose positive or negative coordinates place them in one of four quadrants.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Puntos escritos como (x, y) cuyas coordenadas positivas o negativas los ubican en uno de cuatro cuadrantes.
vocabulary.visual: (−3, 4) is in Quadrant II.
vocabulary.cloze: The ___ of a point's two coordinates decide which quadrant it lands in.

examples.why: Both coordinates negative puts it down and to the left.
Quadrant I needs both coordinates positive.

vocabulary.definition: Flip a point across an axis so it stays the same perpendicular distance from that axis.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Voltear un punto sobre un eje para que quede a la misma distancia perpendicular de ese eje.
vocabulary.visual: Across the x-axis: (3, 2) → (3, −2).
vocabulary.cloze: Reflecting across an axis keeps that coordinate and flips the ___ one.

examples.why: The x stayed; only the y changed sign.
That changed the x, which is a reflection across the y-axis.

vocabulary.definition: A grid with a line going across and a line going up to plot points.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una cuadrícula con una línea horizontal y una vertical para marcar puntos.
vocabulary.visual: A grid with a horizontal line (x-axis) crossing a vertical line (y-axis), making four sections
vocabulary.cloze: The grid made by a horizontal and a vertical number line is the ___.

examples.text: A grid with an x-axis and a y-axis crossing at 0
examples.why: Two number lines that let a pair name one point.
One line can place a number, but not a pair.

vocabulary.definition: How far apart two points are. It is never negative.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan separados están dos puntos. Nunca es negativo.
vocabulary.visual: The distance from -3 to 4 on a number line is |-3| + |4| = 3 + 4 = 7 units
vocabulary.cloze: How far apart two points are on the coordinate plane is the ___.

examples.why: It counts the units between them, so it is positive.
A distance is never negative, whichever way you travelled.

vocabulary.definition: A closed figure made of line segments; on the plane you draw it by plotting the vertices and connecting them in order.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura cerrada hecha de segmentos; en el plano se dibuja marcando los vértices y conectándolos en orden.
vocabulary.example: Plot the four points, connect them, and the rectangle appears.
vocabulary.visual: Plot (2, 4), (5, 4), (5, −4), (2, −4) and join them — a rectangle appears.
vocabulary.cloze: A closed figure made of line segments is a ___.

examples.text: Four plotted vertices joined in order into a closed rectangle
examples.why: Straight sides, and the figure closes.

examples.text: Three points joined but left open
examples.why: An unclosed path is not a polygon.

vocabulary.definition: One of the four parts of a coordinate grid, numbered I to IV.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una de las cuatro partes de una cuadrícula de coordenadas, numeradas I a IV.
vocabulary.visual: I (+, +) top-right, II (-, +) top-left, III (-, -) bottom-left, IV (+, -) bottom-right
vocabulary.cloze: One of the four regions of the coordinate plane, numbered I to IV, is a ___.

examples.why: Negative x and positive y put it up and to the left.
A point on an axis is in no quadrant at all.

vocabulary.definition: A flipped, mirror image across a line.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una imagen reflejada al otro lado de una línea.
vocabulary.visual: (3, 2) reflected over the y-axis becomes (-3, 2) — x changes sign, y stays
vocabulary.cloze: A flip of a point or shape over an axis to make a mirror image is a ___.

examples.why: It is a mirror image across the axis.
That is a slide, not a reflection.

vocabulary.term: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
vocabulary.termEs: Números racionales en la recta numérica
vocabulary.definition: Every rational number has one exact spot on the number line. Writing it as a fraction, a decimal, or an integer does not change where it sits.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cada número racional tiene un lugar exacto en la recta numérica. Escribirlo como fracción, decimal o entero no cambia dónde queda.
vocabulary.visual: −3/2 = −1.5 and 1/2 = 0.5 each sit at one exact point.
vocabulary.cloze: A rational number always has one exact spot on the ___ ___.

examples.why: Its value decides where it goes, not its form.
The digits are not the value — -3/4 is less than one unit from 0.

vocabulary.definition: A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers, with a bottom number that is not zero.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que se puede escribir como una fracción de dos enteros, con un denominador que no sea cero.
vocabulary.visual: −1/2, 0 and 5/4 each sit at one exact point.
vocabulary.cloze: A number you can write as a fraction of two integers, with a bottom number that is not zero, is a ___.

examples.why: It can be written as −3/1 — both parts are integers.
It can be written as 3/4, so it is rational.

vocabulary.definition: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que muestra una parte de un todo, como 3/4.
vocabulary.visual: 3/4 means 3 out of 4 equal parts — like 3 slices of a pizza cut into 4
vocabulary.cloze: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/5, is a ___.

examples.text: -3/4 as a point three-quarters of the way from 0 to -1
examples.why: It names a part of a whole and has a place on the line.
Two separate digits are not a part of a whole.

vocabulary.definition: A coordinate less than zero. It means left or below the center point.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una coordenada menor que cero. Significa a la izquierda o debajo del centro.
vocabulary.visual: (-3, 2) means 3 left and 2 up from the origin
vocabulary.cloze: A coordinate less than zero, which places a point left of or below the origin, is a ___.

examples.why: It is a coordinate less than zero.
5 is positive, not negative.

vocabulary.definition: How far a number is from zero. It is never negative.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Qué tan lejos está un número de cero. Nunca es negativo.
vocabulary.visual: |-3| = 3 and |4| = 4; to find distance: |4 - (-3)| = 7
vocabulary.cloze: The distance of a number from zero, used to find distance between points, is its ___.

examples.why: It measures how far the number is from 0.
Distance cannot be negative, whichever side you started on.

vocabulary.definition: The line that goes across the grid. Flipping over it changes the y sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La línea que va de lado en la cuadrícula. Voltear sobre ella cambia el signo de y.
vocabulary.visual: (4, 3) → (4, -3): the y flips from +3 to -3, like folding the paper along the horizontal line
vocabulary.cloze: The horizontal number line on the coordinate plane is the ___.

examples.why: It runs across, so a flip over it changes the y sign.
Changing x is a flip over the y-axis instead.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se cruzan formando una esquina cuadrada (90 grados).
vocabulary.visual: The dashed height meets the base at a square corner — the small 90° box is what makes it perpendicular, not slanted.
vocabulary.cloze: Two lines that meet at a 90° square corner are ___.

examples.text: The x-axis and the y-axis where they cross
examples.why: They meet at a square corner.

examples.text: Two grid lines running the same direction
examples.why: Parallel lines never meet, so they form no corner.

Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 7.4–7.9
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 7.4: The number farther to the left is always less; the number farther to the right is always greater. • 7.5: Always start at the origin (0, 0), move right/left first, then up/down. • 7.6: If points are on the same side of zero, subtract; if they are on opposite sides of zero, add the absolute values. • 7.7: When two vertices share a coordinate, the side between them is the absolute difference of the coordinates that differ. • 7.8: The signs of (x, y) tell you the quadrant: (+,+) is I, (-,+) is II, (-,-) is III, (+,-) is IV. • 7.9: Reflect over the x-axis: the y-coordinate changes sign. Reflect over the y-axis: the x-coordinate changes sign.

lines: Lesson 7.4 — Compare and Order Integers and Rational Numbers: The number farther to the left is always less; the number farther to the right is always greater.
Lesson 7.5 — Represent Rational Numbers on the Coordinate Plane: Always start at the origin (0, 0), move right/left first, then up/down.
Lesson 7.6 — Determine Distance on the Coordinate Plane: If points are on the same side of zero, subtract; if they are on opposite sides of zero, add the absolute values.
Lesson 7.7 — Represent Polygons on the Coordinate Plane: When two vertices share a coordinate, the side between them is the absolute difference of the coordinates that differ.
Lesson 7.8 — Ordered Pairs in All Four Quadrants: The signs of (x, y) tell you the quadrant: (+,+) is I, (-,+) is II, (-,-) is III, (+,-) is IV.
Lesson 7.9 — Reflect Points Across Axes: Reflect over the x-axis: the y-coordinate changes sign. Reflect over the y-axis: the x-coordinate changes sign.

weDo.title: Quick guided checks — one from each lesson
lines: From 7.4: Now let's compare -2 and 3. Which one is to the left on the number line? The -2 is left of zero.
From 7.5: Now let's plot (2, 1). Where do we start? At the origin (0, 0).
From 7.6: Now let's find the distance from (2, 3) to (2, 8). What do these points share? The same x = 2, so it is a vertical line.
From 7.7: The shape is a rectangle, so the opposite sides match: two sides of 9.5 and two of 6.75.
From 7.8: Now let's plot (-5, 2). The x is -5, so which way do we move? Left 5 units.
From 7.9: Now let's reflect (4, -5) over the x-axis. Which coordinate changes over the x-axis? The y-coordinate.

discourse.prompt: What pattern do you notice about the coordinates when reflecting over the x-axis versus the y-axis?
discourse.sentenceFrame: When I reflect over the x-axis, the ___ -coordinate changes sign and the ___ -coordinate stays the same. When I reflect over the y-axis, the ___ -coordinate changes sign and the ___ -coordinate stays the same.

diagram.title: Reflect the triangle over the y-axis
diagram.caption: Plot triangle A, B, C first, then its reflection A', B', C'. Reflecting over the y-axis flips the sign of x and leaves y alone.

optional.stem: (Lesson 7.4) Four spots: -3 m, 2 m, -7 m, 0 m. Order them from least to greatest.
optional.explanation: The deepest spot is the cave at -7 (farthest left), then the tide pool -3, then the boat deck 0, then the flag at 2. Least to greatest: -7, -3, 0, 2.
choiceFeedback: With negative numbers, the one farther from zero is smaller—-7 is less than -3.
Start at the left (least/smallest) on the number line and move right to the greatest.
Zero is between all negatives and all positives—check its position in your order.
optional.stemEs: Cuatro lugares: -3 m, 2 m, -7 m, 0 m. Ordénalos de menor a mayor.
optional.explanationEs: El lugar más profundo es la cueva en -7 (el más a la izquierda), luego la poza de marea -3, luego la cubierta del barco 0, y luego la bandera en 2. De menor a mayor: -7, -3, 0, 2.
hints: Least to greatest is the same as left to right on the number line.
Sketch a number line with 0 in the middle and place each value: negatives go left of 0 and positives go right.
Place -7 and -3 first — the one farther left comes earlier in the list. Then decide where 0 and 2 fall after them.
hintsEs: De menor a mayor es lo mismo que de izquierda a derecha en la recta numérica.
Dibuja una recta numérica con el 0 en el medio y coloca cada valor: los negativos van a la izquierda del 0 y los positivos a la derecha.
Coloca primero -7 y -3: el que esté más a la izquierda va antes en la lista. Luego decide dónde caen 0 y 2 después de ellos.

optional.stem: (Lesson 7.5) Spot 1 — Captain Vega's first clue says the Sandy Dock is right 7 and up 2 from the origin. Which ordered pair names the Sandy Dock?
optional.explanation: The x-coordinate is the sideways move (right 7) and the y-coordinate is the up move (up 2), so the Sandy Dock is (7, 2).
choiceFeedback: You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
optional.stemEs: Punto 1: la primera pista de la capitana Vega dice que el Muelle de Arena está 7 a la derecha y 2 hacia arriba desde el origen. ¿Qué par ordenado nombra el Muelle de Arena?
optional.explanationEs: La coordenada x es el movimiento hacia los lados (7 a la derecha) y la coordenada y es el movimiento hacia arriba (2 hacia arriba), así que el Muelle de Arena es (7, 2).
hints: An ordered pair is always written (x, y): the sideways number first, the up-and-down number second.
Match each clue word to a coordinate — “right” describes the x-coordinate and “up” describes the y-coordinate.
The clue says right 7, so 7 belongs in the first position. Now decide which number goes in the second position.
hintsEs: Un par ordenado siempre se escribe (x, y): primero el número hacia los lados y después el número hacia arriba o abajo.
Relaciona cada palabra de la pista con una coordenada: «a la derecha» describe la coordenada x y «hacia arriba» describe la coordenada y.
La pista dice 7 a la derecha, así que el 7 va en la primera posición. Ahora decide qué número va en la segunda posición.

optional.stem: (Lesson 7.6) The Bank is at (2, 3) and the Library is at (2, 9). How many blocks apart are they?
optional.explanation: Same x = 2, so the segment is vertical. Distance = |9 - 3| = 6 blocks.
choiceFeedback: 12 adds the two y-values, 3 + 9. Distance along a vertical street is the GAP between them — how far is it from 3 up to 9?
It looks like you used the Bank's y-coordinate, 3, as the answer. A coordinate tells you where a building sits, not how far apart two buildings are — compare 3 with 9.
It looks like you added 2 and 9, which mixes an x-coordinate with a y-coordinate. Both places share x = 2, so the numbers that change are the y-values.
optional.stemEs: El Banco está en (2, 3) y la Biblioteca está en (2, 9). ¿A cuántas cuadras de distancia están?
optional.explanationEs: El mismo x = 2, así que el segmento es vertical. Distancia = |9 - 3| = 6 cuadras.
hints: Both buildings sit at x = 2, so the trip between them runs straight up and down — only the y-coordinates change.
For a vertical trip where both y-values are above zero, subtract them and take the absolute value: |9 - 3|.
Start at y = 3 and count up one block at a time: 3 to 4, 4 to 5, 5 to 6 … keep counting until you land on y = 9.
hintsEs: Los dos edificios están en x = 2, así que el recorrido entre ellos va directo hacia arriba y hacia abajo; solo cambian las coordenadas y.
Para un recorrido vertical donde los dos valores de y están arriba del cero, réstalos y toma el valor absoluto: |9 - 3|.
Empieza en y = 3 y cuenta hacia arriba de cuadra en cuadra: de 3 a 4, de 4 a 5, de 5 a 6… sigue contando hasta llegar a y = 9.

optional.stem: (Lesson 7.8) A sonar ping locates an enemy submarine at (-5, -2). In which quadrant should Captain Vega aim her shot?
optional.explanation: A negative x means left and a negative y means down, so (-5, -2) is in Quadrant III, where both coordinates are negative.
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I is where x is positive and y is positive. Check the sign of each coordinate in the point and match both.
Quadrant II sits above the x-axis, so its y-coordinate is positive, but this ping's y is −2.
Quadrant IV needs a positive x-coordinate, and this ping's x is −5.
optional.stemEs: Un eco de sonar ubica un submarino enemigo en (-5, -2). ¿En qué cuadrante debe apuntar su disparo la capitana Vega?
optional.explanationEs: Una x negativa significa izquierda y una y negativa significa abajo, así que (-5, -2) está en el cuadrante III, donde las dos coordenadas son negativas.
hints: The signs of the two coordinates decide the quadrant: x tells left or right, and y tells up or down.
Check each sign separately, then find the corner of the plane that matches both directions.
In (−5, −2) the x is negative, so move left of the origin; the y is negative, so move down. Name the quadrant those two moves land in.
hintsEs: Los signos de las dos coordenadas deciden el cuadrante: la x indica izquierda o derecha y la y indica arriba o abajo.
Revisa cada signo por separado y después busca la esquina del plano que coincide con las dos direcciones.
En (−5, −2) la x es negativa, así que muévete a la izquierda del origen; la y es negativa, así que muévete hacia abajo. Nombra el cuadrante donde caen esos dos movimientos.

optional.stem: (Lesson 7.9) Captain Vega folds the map along the x-axis. A marker at (7, 2) lands on its mirror image. What are the new coordinates?
optional.explanation: Folding along (reflecting across) the x-axis flips the sign of the y-coordinate only. (7, 2) becomes (7, -2).
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you changed the sign of both coordinates. Instead: Folding along (reflecting across) the x-axis flips the sign of the y-coordinate only.
Both coordinates changed sign, which describes two folds rather than one. Folding along the x-axis changes only one of them.
The coordinates traded places. A reflection keeps x first and y second and only changes a sign.
optional.stemEs: La Capitana Vega dobla el mapa a lo largo del eje x. Un marcador en (7, 2) cae sobre su imagen reflejada. ¿Cuáles son las nuevas coordenadas?
optional.explanationEs: Doblar sobre el eje x (reflejar a través de él) cambia solo el signo de la coordenada y. El punto (7, 2) se convierte en (7, -2).
hints: Folding along an axis makes that axis the mirror line, and the point lands the same distance away on the other side.
The x-axis runs left and right, so the fold moves the point up or down — decide which coordinate that affects.
The marker is 2 units above the x-axis, so its image must be 2 units below it. The first coordinate does not move at all.
hintsEs: Doblar a lo largo de un eje convierte ese eje en la línea espejo, y el punto cae a la misma distancia del otro lado.
El eje x va de izquierda a derecha, así que el doblez mueve el punto hacia arriba o hacia abajo: decide qué coordenada se ve afectada.
El marcador está 2 unidades arriba del eje x, así que su imagen debe estar 2 unidades abajo. La primera coordenada no se mueve.

approaching.explanation: -5 is farther to the left on the number line than -2, so -5 < -2 is true.
choiceFeedback: With negatives, the one farther from zero is less, even though 3 > 1.
Any negative number is less than any positive number—not greater than zero.
Check on the number line: -1 is closer to zero than -6, so -1 > -6.
hints: Sketch a quick number line. For negatives, 'greater' means closer to zero, not a bigger digit.
For each statement, place both numbers on the number line: the one farther LEFT is less. Test all four.
First statement: put -3 and -1 on the line. -3 is farther left, so is '-3 > -1' true or false? Keep testing.
approaching.explanationEs: -5 está más a la izquierda en la recta numérica que -2, así que -5 < -2 es verdadero.
hintsEs: Dibuja una recta numérica rápida. En los negativos, 'mayor' significa más cerca de cero, no un dígito más grande.
Para cada enunciado, coloca ambos números en la recta: el que está más a la IZQUIERDA es menor. Prueba los cuatro.
Primer enunciado: pon −3 y −1 en la recta. −3 está más a la izquierda, entonces ¿'−3 > −1' es verdadero o falso? Sigue probando.

approaching.explanation: -8 is farthest to the left on the number line, making it the least (smallest) integer.
choiceFeedback: The least is the one farthest left on the number line—-8 is farther left than -3.
Any positive or zero is greater than any negative number.
Any positive number is greater than any negative number—check the signs.
hints: 'Least' means farthest LEFT on the number line — for negatives, that's the one farthest below zero.
Place all five numbers on a mental number line. Negatives sit left of 0, and the least is the leftmost one.
Compare just the negatives first, -3 and -8: which is farther below zero? Then check it against 0, 2, and 5.
approaching.explanationEs: -8 está más a la izquierda en la recta numérica, lo que lo hace el entero menor (más pequeño).
hintsEs: 'Menor' significa lo más a la IZQUIERDA en la recta numérica; en los negativos, el que está más abajo de cero.
Coloca los cinco números en una recta numérica mental. Los negativos van a la izquierda de 0 y el menor es el más a la izquierda.
Compara primero los negativos, −3 y −8: ¿cuál está más abajo de cero? Luego compáralo con 0, 2 y 5.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.5) Which ordered pair names a point 3 units right and 7 units up from the origin?
approaching.explanation: The first coordinate is horizontal (right 3), the second is vertical (up 7). So (3, 7).
choiceFeedback: You swapped the x and y—the first number is horizontal, second is vertical.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Re-read the moves: 3 units right, then 7 units up. Which move comes first in an ordered pair?
An ordered pair is (x, y): x is the right/left distance, y is the up/down distance. Match each move to its slot.
Start at the origin and go right 3 — that 3 is the x, the first number. Now decide where the 'up 7' goes.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué par ordenado nombra un punto que está 3 unidades a la derecha y 7 unidades hacia arriba desde el origen?
approaching.explanationEs: La primera coordenada es horizontal (3 a la derecha) y la segunda es vertical (7 hacia arriba). Entonces (3, 7).
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer los movimientos: 3 unidades a la derecha y luego 7 unidades hacia arriba. ¿Cuál movimiento va primero en un par ordenado?
Un par ordenado es (x, y): x es la distancia derecha/izquierda y y es la distancia arriba/abajo. Une cada movimiento con su lugar.
Empieza en el origen y ve 3 a la derecha: ese 3 es la x, el primer número. Ahora decide dónde va el 'arriba 7'.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.5) What are the coordinates of the origin?
approaching.explanation: The origin is where the x-axis and y-axis cross, at (0, 0).
choiceFeedback: The origin is where both axes cross, where both values are zero.
Both coordinates at the origin are 0 — not mixed with 1.
The origin is where the two axes cross each other. At that crossing point, how far along is each axis? That tells you both coordinates.
hints: The origin is the exact spot where the x-axis and y-axis cross. Picture that crossing point.
Ask: how far right have you moved at the origin? How far up? Those two distances are the coordinates.
At the crossing point you haven't moved right at all, so x = 0. Now figure out the y-value the same way.
approaching.explanationEs: El origen es donde se cruzan el eje x y el eje y, en (0, 0).
hintsEs: El origen es el punto exacto donde se cruzan el eje x y el eje y. Imagina ese cruce.
Pregunta: en el origen, ¿cuánto te has movido a la derecha? ¿Y hacia arriba? Esas dos distancias son las coordenadas.
En el punto de cruce no te has movido nada a la derecha, así que x = 0. Ahora halla el valor de y igual.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.6) What is the distance between (-4, 3) and (2, 3)?
approaching.explanation: Both points have y = 3, so this is a horizontal distance. |2 - (-4)| = |2 + 4| = 6 units.
choiceFeedback: 2 is the difference of the sizes 4 and 2, but the points sit on OPPOSITE sides of zero. Count the units from -4 to 0, then from 0 to 2, and combine them.
It looks like you counted from -4 only as far as 0 and stopped there. The segment keeps going past the origin to x = 2, so there are more units to add on.
This is the distance you would get if the second point were at x = 4 instead of x = 2. Find 2 on the x-axis and count only that far.
hints: Both points have y = 3, so they sit on the same horizontal line — only the x-values differ.
Find the gap between x = -4 and x = 2. The path crosses zero, so add the two distances |-4| and |2|.
Count from -4 to 0 (that's 4 units), then from 0 to 2. Add the two parts together.
approaching.explanationEs: Los dos puntos tienen y = 3, así que esta es una distancia horizontal. |2 - (-4)| = |2 + 4| = 6 unidades.
hintsEs: Ambos puntos tienen y = 3, así que están en la misma línea horizontal: solo cambian los valores de x.
Halla la distancia entre x = −4 y x = 2. El camino cruza el cero, así que suma las dos distancias |−4| y |2|.
Cuenta de −4 a 0 (son 4 unidades) y luego de 0 a 2. Suma las dos partes.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.6) What is the distance between (5, -2) and (5, 4)?
approaching.explanation: Both points have x = 5, so this is a vertical distance. |4 - (-2)| = |4 + 2| = 6 units.
choiceFeedback: 2 only counts part of the trip. The segment runs from y = -2 all the way up to y = 4 — the units below zero and above zero both count.
You counted the part above the x-axis, from 0 up to 4, but the segment starts below the axis at -2. Add the units under zero too.
It looks like you combined the x-coordinates (5 and 5) instead of the y-coordinates. The x-values match here, which is the clue that the segment is vertical — the y-values are what change.
hints: Both points share x = 5 — the segment is VERTICAL, so compare the y-values -2 and 4.
The path crosses zero: split it into a below-zero part and an above-zero part using absolute values.
From y = -2 up to 0 is 2 units; from 0 up to 4 is 4 more. Add the parts.
approaching.explanationEs: Los dos puntos tienen x = 5, así que esta es una distancia vertical. |4 - (-2)| = |4 + 2| = 6 unidades.
hintsEs: Ambos puntos comparten x = 5: el segmento es VERTICAL, así que compara los valores de y, −2 y 4.
El camino cruza el cero: divídelo en una parte debajo de cero y otra arriba de cero usando valores absolutos.
De y = −2 hasta 0 son 2 unidades; de 0 hasta 4 son 4 más. Suma las partes.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.7) Vertices (-4.5, 3) and (5, 3) share y = 3. What is the distance between them?
approaching.explanation: They differ only in x: |5 − (−4.5)| = 5 + 4.5 = 9.5 units.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 4.5 − 4 or similar — remember the point is at NEGATIVE 4.5, so the distance crosses zero.
That ignores the .5 on −4.5.
That subtracts 5 − 3.5 or mixes an x with a y — use the two x-coordinates only.
hints: Which coordinate is the same? Which differs?
The x-values are −4.5 and 5.
Distance crosses zero: 4.5 to reach 0, then 5 more.
approaching.stemEs: Los vértices (-4.5, 3) y (5, 3) comparten y = 3. ¿Cuál es la distancia entre ellos?
approaching.explanationEs: Solo se diferencian en x: |5 − (−4.5)| = 5 + 4.5 = 9.5 unidades.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál coordenada es igual? ¿Cuál es distinta?
Los valores de x son −4.5 y 5.
La distancia cruza el cero: 4.5 para llegar a 0, luego 5 más.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.7) Vertices (5, 3) and (5, -3.75) share x = 5. What is the distance between them?
approaching.explanation: They differ only in y: |3 − (−3.75)| = 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 units.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 3.75 − 3 as if both were on the same side of zero.
5 is the shared x-coordinate, not a distance.
That adds 5 + 3.75, mixing the shared x into the answer.
hints: Which coordinate differs?
The y-values are 3 and −3.75.
3 above zero plus 3.75 below zero.
approaching.stemEs: Los vértices (5, 3) y (5, -3.75) comparten x = 5. ¿Cuál es la distancia entre ellos?
approaching.explanationEs: Solo se diferencian en y: |3 − (−3.75)| = 3 + 3.75 = 6.75 unidades.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál coordenada es distinta?
Los valores de y son 3 y −3.75.
3 arriba del cero más 3.75 abajo del cero.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.8) In which quadrant is the point (-4, 5)?
approaching.explanation: The x-coordinate is negative (left) and the y-coordinate is positive (up). Left and up is Quadrant II.
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I is where x is positive and y is positive. Check the sign of each coordinate in the point and match both.
Quadrant III holds points where both coordinates are negative. Here the y-coordinate is 5, which is positive.
Quadrant IV pairs a positive x with a negative y. Look again at the sign of the x-coordinate in (-4, 5).
hints: Look at the signs: x = -4 is negative and y = 5 is positive.
Negative x means move LEFT; positive y means move UP. Ask which corner of the plane is left-and-up.
From the origin, slide left 4 and climb up 5. Quadrants count I, II, III, IV counterclockwise from top-right.
approaching.explanationEs: La coordenada x es negativa (izquierda) y la coordenada y es positiva (arriba). Izquierda y arriba es el cuadrante II.
hintsEs: Mira los signos: x = −4 es negativo y y = 5 es positivo.
Una x negativa significa moverse a la IZQUIERDA; una y positiva significa moverse hacia ARRIBA. Pregunta qué esquina del plano es izquierda y arriba.
Desde el origen, deslízate 4 a la izquierda y sube 5. Los cuadrantes se cuentan I, II, III, IV en sentido antihorario desde arriba a la derecha.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.8) A point has a positive x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate. Which quadrant is it in?
approaching.explanation: Positive x (right) and negative y (down) = Quadrant IV (bottom-right).
choiceFeedback: Quadrant I is where x is positive and y is positive. Check the sign of each coordinate in the point and match both.
Quadrant II needs a negative x-coordinate. This point's x is positive, so it sits on the right side of the plane.
In Quadrant III both coordinates are negative, but only the y-coordinate is negative here.
hints: Positive x pushes you RIGHT; negative y drops you DOWN.
Find the corner that is right of the y-axis and below the x-axis. Quadrants I–IV go counterclockwise from top-right.
Try a sample point like (3, -2): go right 3, then down 2. See which corner of the grid that lands in.
approaching.stemEs: Un punto tiene la coordenada x positiva y la coordenada y negativa. ¿En qué cuadrante está?
approaching.explanationEs: x positiva (derecha) y y negativa (abajo) = cuadrante IV (abajo a la derecha).
hintsEs: Una x positiva te lleva a la DERECHA; una y negativa te baja.
Halla la esquina que está a la derecha del eje y y debajo del eje x. Los cuadrantes I–IV van en sentido antihorario desde arriba a la derecha.
Prueba un punto de ejemplo como (3, −2): ve 3 a la derecha y luego 2 hacia abajo. Mira en qué esquina de la cuadrícula cae.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.9) What is the reflection of (4, -3) over the x-axis?
approaching.explanation: Reflecting over the x-axis changes the sign of the y-coordinate. The x stays the same (4), and the y changes from -3 to 3. The answer is (4, 3).
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you changed the sign of both coordinates. Instead: Reflecting over the x-axis changes the sign of the y-coordinate.
Both coordinates changed sign here, which is what two reflections would do. A single reflection over the x-axis leaves one coordinate untouched — decide which one.
The two numbers traded places. Reflecting never swaps x with y; it only changes a sign.
hints: Reflecting over the x-axis flips the point UP/DOWN — the left/right position doesn't move.
Keep the x-coordinate the same and switch the sign of the y-coordinate. Don't swap the numbers' order.
The point sits 3 units below the x-axis. Its mirror sits the same 3 units above, with the x still 4.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es la reflexión de (4, -3) sobre el eje x?
approaching.explanationEs: Reflejar sobre el eje x cambia el signo de la coordenada y. La x se mantiene igual (4) y la y pasa de -3 a 3. La respuesta es (4, 3).
hintsEs: Reflejar sobre el eje x voltea el punto ARRIBA/ABAJO: la posición izquierda/derecha no se mueve.
Conserva igual la coordenada x y cambia el signo de la coordenada y. No intercambies el orden de los números.
El punto está 3 unidades debajo del eje x. Su reflejo está esas mismas 3 unidades arriba, con la x todavía en 4.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 7.9) What is the reflection of (-2, 6) over the y-axis?
approaching.explanation: Reflecting over the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate. x goes from -2 to 2, and y stays 6. The answer is (2, 6).
choiceFeedback: That is what you get if you changed the sign of both coordinates. Instead: Reflecting over the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate.
Both signs flipped in this point. A reflection over the y-axis changes only one coordinate — think about which one the vertical axis affects.
The coordinates were swapped instead of reflected. Keep x in the first position and y in the second, then change only a sign.
hints: Reflecting over the y-axis flips LEFT/RIGHT — the height stays the same.
Switch the sign of the x-coordinate and keep the y-coordinate 6 unchanged.
The point is 2 units left of the y-axis. Its mirror lands 2 units to the RIGHT, at the same height.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es la reflexión de (-2, 6) sobre el eje y?
approaching.explanationEs: Reflejar sobre el eje y cambia el signo de la coordenada x. La x pasa de -2 a 2 y la y se mantiene en 6. La respuesta es (2, 6).
hintsEs: Reflejar sobre el eje y voltea IZQUIERDA/DERECHA: la altura se queda igual.
Cambia el signo de la coordenada x y conserva la coordenada y en 6 sin cambios.
El punto está 2 unidades a la izquierda del eje y. Su reflejo cae 2 unidades a la DERECHA, a la misma altura.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.4) Three cities have temperatures of -12°F, -5°F, and 3°F. Which city is warmest?
onLevel.explanation: 3°F is the greatest because it is farthest to the right on the number line. The order from coldest to warmest is -12, -5, 3.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. The order from coldest to warmest is -12, -5, ___.
This one is farthest to the left on the number line, which makes it the coldest reading rather than the warmest. Warmer temperatures sit farther right.
The three readings are different numbers, so they cannot describe the same temperature. Place them on a number line and compare their positions.
hints: Warmest = greatest temperature. On a thermometer, greater is higher — farther right on a number line.
Compare positions on a number line: temperatures farther right are warmer. Check where negatives sit versus positives.
Place -12, -5, and 3 on a number line and find the one farthest to the right. That city is warmest.
onLevel.stemEs: Tres ciudades tienen temperaturas de -12°F, -5°F y 3°F. ¿Cuál ciudad es la más cálida?
onLevel.explanationEs: 3°F es la mayor porque está más a la derecha en la recta numérica. El orden del más frío al más cálido es -12, -5, 3.
hintsEs: El más cálido = la temperatura mayor. En un termómetro, mayor es más alto, o sea más a la derecha en una recta numérica.
Compara posiciones en una recta numérica: las temperaturas más a la derecha son más cálidas. Revisa dónde quedan los negativos frente a los positivos.
Coloca −12, −5 y 3 en una recta numérica y halla el más a la derecha. Esa ciudad es la más cálida.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 7.4) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Read
workedExample.work: Order -8 and -15 from least to greatest.
workedExample.workEs: Ordena -8 y -15 de menor a mayor.

workedExample.label: Attempt
workedExample.work: The student wrote -8, -15, because 8 is smaller than 15.
workedExample.workEs: El estudiante escribió -8, -15, porque 8 es menor que 15.

workedExample.label: Check
workedExample.work: -15 is farther left than -8 on the number line, so -15 is the least. The correct order is -15, -8.
workedExample.workEs: -15 está más a la izquierda que -8 en la recta numérica, así que -15 es el menor. El orden correcto es -15, -8.

onLevel.correctWork: Least to greatest: -15, -8. The more negative a number is, the less its value — so -15 < -8.
hints: Which number is farther to the left on the number line?
For negative numbers, a bigger digit can mean a smaller value.
onLevel.explanation: The reasoning treats -8 and -15 like 8 and 15, so it puts -8 first. On the number line -15 sits farther left than -8, which makes it the smaller value, so least to greatest is -15, -8.
onLevel.explanationEs: El razonamiento trata -8 y -15 como si fueran 8 y 15, así que pone -8 primero. En la recta numérica -15 queda más a la izquierda que -8, lo que lo hace el valor menor, así que de menor a mayor es -15, -8.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: De menor a mayor: -15, -8. Cuanto más negativo es un número, menor es su valor — así que -15 < -8.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál número está más a la izquierda en la recta numérica?
En los números negativos, un dígito más grande puede significar un valor menor.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 7.5) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Clue
workedExample.work: Plot the point (4, 0).
workedExample.workEs: Grafica el punto (4, 0).

workedExample.label: Move right
workedExample.work: Move 4 units to the right along the x-axis. Good.
workedExample.workEs: Muévete 4 unidades a la derecha por el eje x. Bien.

workedExample.label: Move up
workedExample.work: Move 4 units up, because the pair has a 4 in it.
workedExample.workEs: Sube 4 unidades, porque el par tiene un 4.

workedExample.label: Plot the point
workedExample.work: Place the dot at (4, 4).
workedExample.workEs: Coloca el punto en (4, 4).

onLevel.correctWork: The y-coordinate is 0, not 4. After moving 4 right, the up move is 0 units, so the point stays on the x-axis at (4, 0). The student reused the x-value instead of reading the second number (0).
hints: What is the SECOND number in (4, 0), and how far up does it tell you to move?
A y-coordinate of 0 means do not move up at all — the point sits right on the x-axis at (4, 0).
onLevel.explanation: The up move comes from the SECOND number, and the second number in (4, 0) is 0. Reusing the 4 pushes the point off the axis to (4, 4). With a y-coordinate of 0 there is no upward move at all, so the point stays right on the x-axis at (4, 0).
onLevel.explanationEs: El movimiento hacia arriba viene del SEGUNDO número, y el segundo número de (4, 0) es 0. Volver a usar el 4 empuja el punto fuera del eje hasta (4, 4). Con una coordenada y igual a 0 no hay ningún movimiento hacia arriba, así que el punto se queda justo sobre el eje x en (4, 0).
onLevel.correctWorkEs: La coordenada y es 0, no 4. Después de moverte 4 a la derecha, la subida es de 0 unidades, así que el punto se queda sobre el eje x en (4, 0). El estudiante reutilizó el valor de x en lugar de leer el segundo número (0).
hintsEs: ¿Cuál es el SEGUNDO número de (4, 0), y cuánto te dice que subas?
Una coordenada y de 0 significa no subir nada — el punto queda justo sobre el eje x en (4, 0).

onLevel.label: (Lesson 7.5) Plot these points to reveal a hidden shape: (1, 1), (1, 5), (6, 5), (6, 1)
onLevel.hint: Start at the origin (0, 0) for each point. Move right first, then up.
hints: Each pair is (x, y). For point A(1, 1) both moves are just 1 unit.
For every point: start at (0, 0), slide right x units along the bottom, then climb up y units.
Plot A first: right 1, up 1. Then B(1, 5): same x, so it sits straight above A — count up to 5.
onLevel.explanation: Each point starts at the origin, moves right the x amount, then up the y amount: A(1, 1), B(1, 5), C(6, 5), D(6, 1). A and B share x = 1, so B sits straight above A, and B and C share y = 5, so they line up across. Connected in order, the four points form a rectangle 5 units wide and 4 units tall.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada punto empieza en el origen, avanza a la derecha la cantidad de x y luego sube la cantidad de y: A(1, 1), B(1, 5), C(6, 5), D(6, 1). A y B comparten x = 1, así que B queda justo arriba de A, y B y C comparten y = 5, así que quedan alineados horizontalmente. Al unirlos en orden, los cuatro puntos forman un rectángulo de 5 unidades de ancho y 4 de alto.
hintsEs: Cada par es (x, y). Para el punto A(1, 1) los dos movimientos son de solo 1 unidad.
Para cada punto: empieza en (0, 0), avanza x unidades a la derecha por abajo y luego sube y unidades.
Ubica primero A: 1 a la derecha, 1 hacia arriba. Luego B(1, 5): la misma x, así que queda justo encima de A — cuenta hasta 5.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.6) Two points are at (-3, -7) and (-3, 5). What is the distance between them?
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Distance = |5 - (-7)| = |5 + 7| = ___.
You counted the part below the x-axis, from -7 up to 0, and stopped. The second point is at y = 5, which is above the axis, so there is more to count.
It looks like you combined -3 with 5 — that mixes an x-coordinate with a y-coordinate. Both points share x = -3, so the numbers that change are the y-values.
hints: Both points share x = -3, so this is a vertical distance between y = -7 and y = 5.
The y-values have opposite signs, so add their absolute values instead of just subtracting the digits.
Count from -7 up to 0 (that's 7 units), then from 0 up to 5. Add the two counts.
onLevel.stemEs: Dos puntos están en (-3, -7) y (-3, 5). ¿Cuál es la distancia entre ellos?
hintsEs: Ambos puntos comparten x = −3, así que esta es una distancia vertical entre y = −7 y y = 5.
Los valores de y tienen signos opuestos, así que suma sus valores absolutos en vez de solo restar los dígitos.
Cuenta de −7 hasta 0 (son 7 unidades) y luego de 0 hasta 5. Suma los dos conteos.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 7.6) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Find the distance between (-5, 2) and (3, 2).
workedExample.workEs: Encuentra la distancia entre (-5, 2) y (3, 2).

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: Both share y = 2, so subtract the x-values: 5 - 3 = 2.
workedExample.workEs: Ambos comparten y = 2, así que resta los valores de x: 5 - 3 = 2.

workedExample.label: Student answer
workedExample.work: The distance is 2 units.
workedExample.workEs: La distancia es 2 unidades.

onLevel.correctWork: The student dropped the negative sign and used 5 instead of -5. The point is at x = -5, so the two points sit on opposite sides of zero. Add the absolute values: |-5| + |3| = 5 + 3 = 8 units. (You can also write |3 - (-5)| = |3 + 5| = 8.) The correct distance is 8 units, not 2.
hints: The first x-coordinate is -5, not 5. Did the student keep the negative sign?
The points are on opposite sides of zero, so add: |-5| + |3| = ___.
onLevel.explanation: The student-thinking step dropped the negative sign and treated -5 as 5. Because the points really sit on opposite sides of the y-axis, the distance is |-5| + |3| = 8 units, which matches |3 - (-5)| = |3 + 5| = 8.
onLevel.explanationEs: En el paso del razonamiento del estudiante se perdió el signo negativo y se trató -5 como 5. Como los puntos en realidad están en lados opuestos del eje y, la distancia es |-5| + |3| = 8 unidades, que coincide con |3 - (-5)| = |3 + 5| = 8.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El estudiante perdió el signo negativo y usó 5 en lugar de -5. El punto está en x = -5, así que los dos puntos quedan en lados opuestos del cero. Suma los valores absolutos: |-5| + |3| = 5 + 3 = 8 unidades. (También puedes escribir |3 - (-5)| = |3 + 5| = 8.) La distancia correcta es 8 unidades, no 2.
hintsEs: La primera coordenada x es -5, no 5. ¿El estudiante conservó el signo negativo?
Los puntos están en lados opuestos del cero, así que suma: |-5| + |3| = ___.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.7) The park's marked vertices are 3 units apart and each unit is 100 feet. What is the park's width?
choiceFeedback: 3 is the number of UNITS — the scale turns units into feet.
That adds 3 + 100 instead of multiplying.
That multiplies by 10 instead of 100.
hints: What does one unit stand for?
Each unit is 100 feet.
onLevel.stemEs: Los vértices marcados del parque están a 3 unidades de distancia y cada unidad son 100 pies. ¿Cuál es el ancho del parque?
hintsEs: ¿Qué representa una unidad?
Cada unidad son 100 pies.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.7) The park's area must be 240,000 sq ft and its width is 300 ft. What is its length?
choiceFeedback: That divides by 3 instead of 300 — keep the zeros with the width.
720 comes from 240,000 ÷ 333 or a slip; recompute 240,000 ÷ 300.
That adds the width to the area — area and length combine by division here.
hints: Area = length × width. Solve for length.
24,000 ÷ 30 is the same division.
onLevel.stemEs: El área del parque debe ser 240,000 pies cuadrados y su ancho es 300 pies. ¿Cuál es su largo?
hintsEs: Área = largo × ancho. Despeja el largo.
24,000 ÷ 30 es la misma división.

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.8) Point A is at (-5, 3). If you move 8 units to the right, what are the new coordinates?
onLevel.explanation: Moving right means adding to the x-coordinate: -5 + 8 = 3. The y stays the same. New point: (3, 3).
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Moving right means adding to the x-coordinate: -5 + 8 = ___.
Remember the x-coordinate tells you how far horizontally.
The first number is the horizontal (right/left) distance.
hints: Moving right changes ONLY the x-coordinate. The y-coordinate stays at 3.
Add the move to the x-value: take -5 and count up 8. Careful crossing zero — use a number line if it helps.
Start at -5 and count 8 steps right: -4, -3, -2, ... keep going all 8 steps. Then keep the y as 3.
onLevel.stemEs: El punto A está en (-5, 3). Si te mueves 8 unidades a la derecha, ¿cuáles son las nuevas coordenadas?
onLevel.explanationEs: Moverse a la derecha significa sumar a la coordenada x: -5 + 8 = 3. La y se queda igual. Punto nuevo: (3, 3).
hintsEs: Moverse a la derecha cambia SOLO la coordenada x. La coordenada y se queda en 3.
Suma el movimiento al valor de x: toma −5 y cuenta 8 hacia arriba. Cuidado al cruzar el cero; usa una recta numérica si ayuda.
Empieza en −5 y cuenta 8 pasos a la derecha: −4, −3, −2, … sigue los 8 pasos. Luego conserva la y como 3.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 7.8) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Name the quadrant for the point (6, -1).
workedExample.workEs: Nombra el cuadrante del punto (6, -1).

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: I'll read the coordinates as (y, x), so I treat this like (-1, 6): the first number -1 is negative (left) and the second number 6 is positive (up).
workedExample.workEs: Leeré las coordenadas como (y, x), así que lo trato como (-1, 6): el primer número -1 es negativo (izquierda) y el segundo número 6 es positivo (arriba).

workedExample.label: Student answer
workedExample.work: (6, -1) is in Quadrant II.
workedExample.workEs: (6, -1) está en el Cuadrante II.

onLevel.correctWork: The order was reversed. In an ordered pair (x, y), x ALWAYS comes first. Here x = 6 (positive → right) and y = -1 (negative → down). Right and down is Quadrant IV, not Quadrant II.
hints: In (6, -1), which number is the x-coordinate — the first or the second?
x = 6 (positive → right) and y = -1 (negative → down). Right and down land you in which quadrant?
onLevel.explanation: An ordered pair is always (x, y), so the first number is the horizontal move and the order cannot be swapped. Here x = 6 sends you right and y = -1 sends you down, which is the bottom-right region — Quadrant IV. Reading it as (-1, 6) described a completely different point.
onLevel.explanationEs: Un par ordenado siempre es (x, y), así que el primer número es el movimiento horizontal y el orden no se puede intercambiar. Aquí x = 6 te manda a la derecha y y = -1 te manda hacia abajo, que es la región inferior derecha: el Cuadrante IV. Leerlo como (-1, 6) describía un punto completamente distinto.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El orden se invirtió. En un par ordenado (x, y), la x SIEMPRE va primero. Aquí x = 6 (positiva → derecha) y y = -1 (negativa → abajo). Derecha y abajo es el Cuadrante IV, no el II.
hintsEs: En (6, -1), ¿cuál número es la coordenada x — el primero o el segundo?
x = 6 (positiva → derecha) y y = -1 (negativa → abajo). A la derecha y hacia abajo caes en ¿cuál cuadrante?

onLevel.stem: (Lesson 7.9) Point A is at (-3, 5). It is reflected over the x-axis to A', then A' is reflected over the y-axis to A''. What are the coordinates of A''?
onLevel.explanation: Over x-axis: (-3, 5) → (-3, -5). Then over y-axis: (-3, -5) → (3, -5). Both coordinates changed sign.
choiceFeedback: The first coordinate at origin is not 1.
Both coordinates at origin are the same value — 0.
One coordinate is correct, but check the other.
hints: Two flips happen in a row — do them one at a time, not both at once.
The first flip (x-axis) changes only the y sign. Then flip THAT result over the y-axis, changing only the x sign.
Step 1: (-3, 5) over the x-axis — keep the -3 and flip the 5. Carry that new point into the second reflection.
onLevel.stemEs: El punto A está en (-3, 5). Se refleja sobre el eje x hasta A', y luego A' se refleja sobre el eje y hasta A''. ¿Cuáles son las coordenadas de A''?
onLevel.explanationEs: Sobre el eje x: (-3, 5) → (-3, -5). Luego sobre el eje y: (-3, -5) → (3, -5). Ambas coordenadas cambiaron de signo.
hintsEs: Ocurren dos reflexiones seguidas: hazlas una a la vez, no las dos juntas.
La primera reflexión (eje x) cambia solo el signo de y. Luego refleja ESE resultado sobre el eje y, cambiando solo el signo de x.
Paso 1: (−3, 5) sobre el eje x — conserva el −3 y cambia el 5. Lleva ese punto nuevo a la segunda reflexión.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 7.9) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Reflect the point (-3, -8) over the x-axis.
workedExample.workEs: Refleja el punto (-3, -8) sobre el eje x.

workedExample.label: Attempt
workedExample.work: Both coordinates are negative, so I will flip the x-coordinate: -3 becomes 3. The answer is (3, -8).
workedExample.workEs: Ambas coordenadas son negativas, así que cambiaré la coordenada x: -3 se convierte en 3. La respuesta es (3, -8).

workedExample.label: Check
workedExample.work: Folding over the horizontal x-axis should send the point up across the axis, but this answer kept it below the axis.
workedExample.workEs: Plegar sobre el eje x horizontal debería mandar el punto hacia arriba cruzando el eje, pero esta respuesta lo dejó debajo del eje.

onLevel.correctWork: Reflecting over the x-axis changes the y-coordinate, not the x-coordinate. The rule is (x, y) -> (x, -y). For (-3, -8), keep x as -3 and flip y: -8 becomes 8. The correct reflection is (-3, 8), not (3, -8). The negative signs do not change which coordinate flips — the axis does.
hints: The x-axis is the horizontal line. Folding over it moves a point up or down, so the y-coordinate is what changes sign.
Over the x-axis: (x, y) -> (x, -y). So (-3, -8) becomes (-3, 8), not (3, -8).
onLevel.explanation: The Attempt step flips the x-coordinate because both numbers are negative, but the signs of the coordinates never decide which one flips — the axis does. Over the x-axis the rule is (x, y) → (x, -y), so (-3, -8) reflects to (-3, 8), moving up across the horizontal axis.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso Intento cambia la coordenada x porque los dos números son negativos, pero los signos de las coordenadas nunca deciden cuál cambia: lo decide el eje. Sobre el eje x la regla es (x, y) → (x, -y), así que (-3, -8) se refleja en (-3, 8) y sube cruzando el eje horizontal.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Reflejar sobre el eje x cambia la coordenada y, no la x. La regla es (x, y) -> (x, -y). Para (-3, -8), conserva la x como -3 y cambia la y: -8 se convierte en 8. La reflexión correcta es (-3, 8), no (3, -8). Los signos negativos no deciden cuál coordenada cambia — lo decide el eje.
hintsEs: El eje x es la línea horizontal. Doblar sobre él mueve un punto hacia arriba o hacia abajo, así que la coordenada y es la que cambia de signo.
Sobre el eje x: (x, y) -> (x, -y). Así que (-3, -8) se convierte en (-3, 8), no en (3, -8).

extending.title: (Lesson 7.4) Find the Comparison Error

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Compare -3 and -8. Which is greater?
workedExample.workEs: Compara -3 y -8. ¿Cuál es mayor?

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: 8 is bigger than 3, so -8 must be greater than -3
workedExample.workEs: 8 es mayor que 3, así que -8 debe ser mayor que -3

extending.correctWork: With negative numbers, the number closer to zero is GREATER. -3 is closer to zero than -8, so -3 > -8. The student compared the digits without considering that negatives work in the opposite direction.
hints: Plot -3 and -8 on a number line. Which one is farther to the right?
For negatives, closer to zero means greater. -3 is only 3 units from zero, but -8 is 8 units away.
extending.explanation: The student's reasoning stops at the digits: because 8 > 3, they concluded -8 > -3. Distance from zero works in the opposite direction for negatives, so -3, which is only 3 units below zero, is greater than -8, which is 8 units below, making the correct statement -3 > -8.
extending.explanationEs: El razonamiento del estudiante se queda en los dígitos: como 8 > 3, concluyó que -8 > -3. La distancia desde cero funciona al revés con los negativos, así que -3, que está solo 3 unidades por debajo de cero, es mayor que -8, que está 8 unidades por debajo, y el enunciado correcto es -3 > -8.
extending.correctWorkEs: Con números negativos, el más cercano al cero es el MAYOR. -3 está más cerca del cero que -8, así que -3 > -8. El estudiante comparó los dígitos sin considerar que con negativos el orden va en dirección opuesta.
hintsEs: Ubica -3 y -8 en una recta numérica. ¿Cuál queda más a la derecha?
En los negativos, estar más cerca del cero significa ser mayor. -3 está a solo 3 unidades del cero, pero -8 está a 8.

extending.title: (Lesson 7.5) Miscounted Grid Lines

workedExample.label: Move along the x-axis
workedExample.work: Start at the origin (0, 0) and count 7 units to the right.
workedExample.workEs: Empieza en el origen (0, 0) y cuenta 7 unidades a la derecha.

workedExample.label: Move along the y-axis
workedExample.work: Count up from the x-axis: 1, 2, 3, 4 — stop on 4.
workedExample.workEs: Cuenta hacia arriba desde el eje x: 1, 2, 3, 4 — detente en 4.

workedExample.label: Plot the point
workedExample.work: Place the dot at (7, 4).
workedExample.workEs: Coloca el punto en (7, 4).

extending.correctWork: The x-axis itself is 0, not 1. Counting up correctly: 1, 2, 3 — the third count lands on y = 3, so the point is (7, 3), not (7, 4). The student started counting one gridline too high by treating the x-axis as unit 1 instead of unit 0.
hints: When you count up from the x-axis, is the x-axis itself unit 0 or unit 1?
The x-axis is 0. The first line above it is 1, the second is 2, the third is 3. So 3 units up lands on y = 3, not y = 4.
extending.titleEs: Líneas de la cuadrícula mal contadas
extending.explanation: Counting up has to start with the x-axis as 0, not 1. The first line above the x-axis is 1, the second is 2, and the third is 3, so 3 units up lands on y = 3. Treating the axis itself as unit 1 pushes every count one gridline too high, which is how (7, 3) turned into (7, 4).
extending.explanationEs: Al contar hacia arriba hay que tomar el eje x como 0, no como 1. La primera línea arriba del eje x es 1, la segunda es 2 y la tercera es 3, así que 3 unidades hacia arriba caen en y = 3. Tratar el eje mismo como la unidad 1 corre toda la cuenta una línea de más, y así (7, 3) se convirtió en (7, 4).
extending.correctWorkEs: El propio eje x es 0, no 1. Contando bien hacia arriba: 1, 2, 3 — el tercer conteo cae en y = 3, así que el punto es (7, 3), no (7, 4). El estudiante empezó a contar una línea de más al tratar el eje x como la unidad 1 en lugar de la unidad 0.
hintsEs: Cuando cuentas hacia arriba desde el eje x, ¿el eje x mismo es la unidad 0 o la unidad 1?
El eje x es 0. La primera línea arriba de él es 1, la segunda es 2, la tercera es 3. Así que 3 unidades hacia arriba caen en y = 3, no en y = 4.

extending.title: (Lesson 7.6) Find the Distance Error

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Find the distance between (-3, 4) and (5, 4)
workedExample.workEs: Encuentra la distancia entre (-3, 4) y (5, 4)

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: Subtract: 5 - 3 = 2
workedExample.workEs: Resta: 5 - 3 = 2

workedExample.label: Student answer
workedExample.work: The distance is 2 units
workedExample.workEs: La distancia es 2 unidades

extending.correctWork: The student subtracted 5 - 3, but the first x-coordinate is -3, not 3. The correct calculation is |5 - (-3)| = |5 + 3| = 8 units. When points span opposite sides of an axis, you must add the absolute values: |-3| + |5| = 3 + 5 = 8.
hints: The student dropped the negative sign on -3. What is the actual difference between -3 and 5?
Try counting on the number line from -3 to 5. How many units is that?
extending.explanation: The subtraction step used 3 in place of -3, so the negative sign disappeared. Keeping it gives |5 - (-3)| = |5 + 3| = 8 units, which is the same as adding the absolute values |-3| + |5| = 3 + 5 = 8 because the points straddle the y-axis.
extending.explanationEs: En el paso de la resta se usó 3 en lugar de -3, así que el signo negativo desapareció. Al conservarlo se obtiene |5 - (-3)| = |5 + 3| = 8 unidades, lo mismo que sumar los valores absolutos |-3| + |5| = 3 + 5 = 8, porque los puntos quedan a ambos lados del eje y.
extending.correctWorkEs: El estudiante restó 5 - 3, pero la primera coordenada x es -3, no 3. El cálculo correcto es |5 - (-3)| = |5 + 3| = 8 unidades. Cuando los puntos cruzan lados opuestos de un eje, debes sumar los valores absolutos: |-3| + |5| = 3 + 5 = 8.
hintsEs: El estudiante perdió el signo negativo del -3. ¿Cuál es la verdadera diferencia entre -3 y 5?
Prueba contar en la recta numérica de -3 a 5. ¿Cuántas unidades son?

extending.stem: (Lesson 7.7) Maria is choosing between two store spaces on a grid where each unit is 1 foot and each grid line is 5 feet apart. Space A is a rectangle 25 ft by 40 ft; Space B is 30 ft by 30 ft. Which has more floor area?
choices: Space A — 1,000 sq ft vs 900 sq ft
Space B — 900 sq ft vs 850 sq ft
Space B — because a square always beats a rectangle
extending.explanation: A: 25 × 40 = 1,000 sq ft. B: 30 × 30 = 900 sq ft. Space A has 100 more square feet.
choiceFeedback: B is 900, but A is 1,000 — recompute 25 × 40.
Shape does not decide area; the dimensions do.
hints: Compute each area.
extending.stemEs: María escoge entre dos locales en una cuadrícula donde cada unidad es 1 pie y cada línea está a 5 pies de distancia. El espacio A es un rectángulo de 25 pies por 40 pies; el espacio B es de 30 pies por 30 pies. ¿Cuál tiene más área de piso?
extending.explanationEs: A: 25 × 40 = 1,000 pies cuadrados. B: 30 × 30 = 900 pies cuadrados. El espacio A tiene 100 pies cuadrados más.
hintsEs: Calcula cada área.
choicesEs: Espacio A — 1,000 pies cuadrados vs 900 pies cuadrados
Espacio B — 900 pies cuadrados vs 850 pies cuadrados
Espacio B — porque un cuadrado siempre le gana a un rectángulo

extending.title: (Lesson 7.8) Find the Quadrant Error

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Identify the quadrant for (-3, -5)
workedExample.workEs: Identifica el cuadrante de (-3, -5)

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: The x is -3, so I go left 3. The y is -5, so I go up 5.
workedExample.workEs: La x es -3, así que voy 3 a la izquierda. La y es -5, así que subo 5.

workedExample.label: Student answer
workedExample.work: (-3, -5) is in Quadrant II
workedExample.workEs: (-3, -5) está en el Cuadrante II

extending.correctWork: A negative y-coordinate means DOWN, not up. Go left 3 and DOWN 5. The point (-3, -5) is in Quadrant III (both negative), not Quadrant II.
hints: What direction does a NEGATIVE y-coordinate go — up or down?
Both coordinates are negative. In which quadrant are both x and y negative?
extending.explanation: A negative y-coordinate means down, not up. From the origin you go left 3 and DOWN 5, landing in the bottom-left region. Both coordinates are negative, and (-, -) is Quadrant III, not Quadrant II.
extending.explanationEs: Una coordenada y negativa significa hacia abajo, no hacia arriba. Desde el origen te mueves 3 a la izquierda y 5 hacia ABAJO, y caes en la región inferior izquierda. Las dos coordenadas son negativas, y (-, -) es el Cuadrante III, no el Cuadrante II.
extending.correctWorkEs: Una coordenada y negativa significa hacia ABAJO, no hacia arriba. Ve 3 a la izquierda y 5 hacia ABAJO. El punto (-3, -5) está en el Cuadrante III (ambas negativas), no en el II.
hintsEs: ¿En qué dirección va una coordenada y NEGATIVA — hacia arriba o hacia abajo?
Ambas coordenadas son negativas. ¿En cuál cuadrante x e y son negativas?

extending.title: (Lesson 7.9) Find the Reflection Error

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Reflect (-3, 5) over the y-axis
workedExample.workEs: Refleja (-3, 5) sobre el eje y

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: The y-axis is vertical, so I change the y-coordinate
workedExample.workEs: El eje y es vertical, así que cambio la coordenada y

extending.correctWork: Reflecting over the y-axis changes the x-coordinate, not the y-coordinate. The correct reflection of (-3, 5) over the y-axis is (3, 5). The student confused which coordinate changes for each axis.
hints: The y-AXIS is the vertical line. Points flip ACROSS it, meaning they move left/right. Which coordinate controls left/right?
Over the y-axis: change x. Over the x-axis: change y. The name of the axis tells you which coordinate STAYS the same.
extending.explanation: The student's thinking step says the vertical y-axis changes the y-coordinate, but the axis name tells you which coordinate stays the same. Over the y-axis the rule is (x, y) → (-x, y), so (-3, 5) reflects to (3, 5), not (-3, -5).
extending.explanationEs: El paso del razonamiento del estudiante dice que el eje y vertical cambia la coordenada y, pero el nombre del eje te dice cuál coordenada se queda igual. Sobre el eje y la regla es (x, y) → (-x, y), así que (-3, 5) se refleja en (3, 5), no en (-3, -5).
extending.correctWorkEs: Reflejar sobre el eje y cambia la coordenada x, no la y. La reflexión correcta de (-3, 5) sobre el eje y es (3, 5). El estudiante confundió cuál coordenada cambia con cada eje.
hintsEs: El EJE Y es la línea vertical. Los puntos se voltean A TRAVÉS de él, o sea que se mueven izquierda/derecha. ¿Cuál coordenada controla izquierda/derecha?
Sobre el eje y: cambia x. Sobre el eje x: cambia y. El nombre del eje te dice qué coordenada SE QUEDA igual.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Reflect Points Across Axes is flipping the sign of the wrong coordinate — changing the x-coordinate when reflecting over the x-axis, instead of the y-coordinate (or vice versa for the y-axis). For example, to reflect (3, -5) over the x-axis, a student might flip the x-coordinate and write (-3, -5), but reflecting over the x-axis only changes the sign of the y-coordinate: (3, -5) becomes (3, 5). Before you submit, ask: 'Did I flip the sign of the coordinate that matches the axis I'm reflecting over — y for the x-axis, x for the y-axis?'

diagram.title: Symmetric Enemy Ship Placement
diagram.caption: The ship sits at (3, 2); reflecting over the y-axis flips x to (-3, 2) and reflecting over the x-axis flips y to (3, -2) — each enemy is the same distance across its axis.

connect.scenario: A game designer creates a spaceship at (3, 2) and wants to place enemy ships as reflections to make the level symmetric. One enemy is reflected over the y-axis, and another is reflected over the x-axis.
connect.promptQuestion: How do reflections help the game designer create a balanced, symmetric level?
connect.prompt: The enemy reflected over the y-axis is at ___ because ___. The enemy reflected over the x-axis is at ___ because ___. Reflections help game designers because ___.

check.stem: Where is the ship after reflecting (3, 2) over the y-axis?
check.explanation: The y-axis is a vertical mirror, so only the x-coordinate flips sign: (3, 2) → (−3, 2).

check.stem: Where is the ship after reflecting (3, 2) over the x-axis?
check.explanation: The x-axis is a horizontal mirror, so only the y-coordinate flips sign: (3, 2) → (3, −2).

check.stem: Reflecting over the y-axis changes which coordinate?
check.explanation: A reflection across the y-axis moves a point left-to-right across a vertical line, so its horizontal position (x) flips while its height (y) stays the same.

connect.modelAnswer: Reflecting (3, 2) over the y-axis flips the x-coordinate to give (−3, 2). Reflecting over the x-axis flips the y-coordinate to give (3, −2). Each enemy ends up the same distance from its axis as the original ship, which is what makes the level look balanced and symmetric.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 7.6) What is the distance between the points (3, -2) and (3, 5)?
exitTicket.explanation: Both points share x = 3, so this is a vertical distance. |5 - (-2)| = |5 + 2| = 7 units.
choiceFeedback: The x-values match — find the gap between the y-values.
Count from -2 up to 5 on the y-axis — don't skip zero.
Find |5 − (-2)| — recount the distance between -2 and 5.
hints: Both points share x = 3, so the distance runs straight up the grid between y = -2 and y = 5.
The y-values sit on opposite sides of zero, so combine their distances from zero rather than subtracting 5 − 2.
Count from y = -2 up to 0 (2 units), then from 0 up to 5 (5 units). Add the parts.
